chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me that Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abi Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My father narrated from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them).
That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) taught his companions in one assembly four hundred topics, each of which is beneficial for a Muslim in his religion and worldly life.
He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, blood-letting (hijama) corrects the body and strengthens the intellect.
And putting perfume on the moustache is from the character of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the honor of the Recorders (Kiraman Katibin).
And using the miswak (tooth-stick) is from the pleasures of God, the Exalted and Glorious, and the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it perfumes the mouth.
And oil softens the skin, increases the brain, facilitates the flow of fluids, removes dryness, and brightens the skin and brightens the complexion.
And washing the head removes dirt and eliminates dust.
And gargling and sniffing water are Sunnah and purification for the mouth and nose.
And snuff clears the head, purifies the body, and alleviates all headaches.
And depilatory powder/cream is a spreader (of hair removal) and purification for the body.
Keeping shoes in good condition is protection for the body and assistance for purity and prayer.
And trimming the nails prevents the greatest disease, increases sustenance, and brings it about.
And plucking the armpits eliminates the bad odor, and it is purity and Sunnah from what the Pure One (peace be upon him) ordered.
And washing the hands before and after food increases sustenance, removes grease from clothes, and clarifies the sight.
And standing in night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl) is health for the body, pleasure for the Lord, the Exalted and Glorious, an approach to mercy, and holding fast to the character of the Prophets.
And eating apples is good for the stomach.
And chewing gum strengthens the teeth, eliminates phlegm, and removes the odor of the mouth.
And sitting in the mosque after dawn until sunrise is faster in seeking sustenance than traveling the earth.
And eating quince strengthens the weak heart, purifies the stomach, increases the strength of the heart/mind, encourages the coward, and improves the child.
And eating twenty-one red raisins every morning on an empty stomach repels all diseases except the disease of death.
ai.seo_question: What are the four hundred beneficial teachings of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding health and daily life?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) holistic approach to *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine), integrating physical hygiene with spiritual discipline. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that mundane acts like grooming and diet are not merely biological necessities but acts of worship (*ibadat*) that purify the body and prepare it for divine connection, reflecting the unity of body and soul in Islamic practice.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 27-1 (The compiler of the book said) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtayni, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather Al-Hassan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB)

that in an assembly the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) taught his companions four-hundred things each of which is very useful for a Muslim’s life and religion. What he (MGB) taught is as follows.
Blood-letting improves physical health and strengthens the intellect.
Putting perfume on the moustache is one of the traditions of the Prophet (MGB) and of the Honorable Recorders (Kiraman Katibin) .
Brushing the teeth is one of the things that pleases the Honorable the Exalted God. It is also one of the traditions of God’s Prophet (MGB). It cleans the mouth.
Soap makes the cuticle soft, increases intelligence, facilitates the flow of water in the body, takes away dryness of the skin and improves the color of the face.
Washing the head takes away dirtiness and cleans dust and rubbish.
Gargling with water and pulling water up into the nose is a tradition. It cleans both the mouth and the nose.
Drawing snuff into the nose clears up the head, cleans the body and alleviates any headaches.
Applying depilatory cream or powder brings happiness and cleans the body.
Keeping the shoes in proper order helps maintain the body and helps with cleanliness and prayer.
Cutting the nails prevents major ailments, increases one’s sustenance and expedites the arrival of one’s share of daily bread.
Shaving the underarm fights bad odor. It is a part of cleanliness and a custom which the clean Prophet (MGB) has ordered.
Washing the hands before and after every meal causes an increase in one’s share of daily bread. It also prevents one’s clothes from getting oily and improves one’s sight.

Staying up at night (to worship God) would improve your health, cause the pleasure of the Honorable the Exalted Lord, is a means of seeking His Mercy, and is a way of following behavior of the Prophets.
Eating an apple is good for the stomach.
Chewing gum would strengthen the teeth, eliminate phlegm and remove bad odor of the mouth.
It is much better to sit in the mosque after dawn until sunrise than to go around and work to earn a living.
Eating quinces would strengthen a weak heart, clean the stomach, improve spiritual strength, convert a scared person to a brave one, and result in the production of a better child.
Eating twenty-one raisins with breakfast every morning would cure all the pains except death.
